sourceInformation.source: Dodge ’Em (Atari, 1980), designed and programmed by Carla Meninsky.
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade maze racing and score attack
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer with WebGPU and automatic WebGL2 fallback; Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio API; Pointer Events; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded miniature night circuit, three-band toon lighting, ink outlines, warm printed-poster typography and cream/gold/teal colors.
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and keyframe tracks for suspension, rolling wheels, gate hops, crash spins, gold tumbling, flags and marquee; procedural vehicle paths and particles.
sourceInformation.audio: Code-only Web Audio: engine synthesis, gold ticks, crash noise, close-call glides, ink-slip effects, original sequenced garage groove at 10% music volume by default, formant-filtered gibberish pit-crew voices. No audio files.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub ghost races for 1–4 players, progress and results; standalone room-code WebRTC ghost races through PeerJS with same-browser BroadcastChannel fallback; two-player local role-swapping couch duel.
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium with software WebGPU; scripted full campaign and state assertions; standard Gamepad API stubs; phone multitouch emulation; Web Audio analyser; official AI Hub harness with 2 and 4 players, 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter, 5% packet loss and host leaving; file:// startup; WebGL2 visual captures. Physical controller/listening/real phone/remote human tests: unknown. Desktop visual review at 1920×1080 and portrait phone captures; controller and touch scrolling verified.
sourceInformation.research: Atari’s original instructions and original manual: four lanes, automatic counterclockwise player, clockwise opponents, gap-only shifts, acceleration, three turns, escalating enemies and role-swapping multiplayer; Atari Archive historical/screenshots context; written source-sound descriptions. Exact original audio waveform: unknown.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux, Ubuntu on WSL2

testingFeedback: 10 issues fixed: six game/UI issues (title alignment, HUD overlap, portrait framing, controller focus, spawn visibility and title warmup timing) and four test-fixture issues (hidden selectors, timing races, touch targeting and gamepad sampling). Full regression: 73/73 passed. Final UI and input recheck: 22/22 passed.
1: the initial portrait framing could hide outer lanes on phones. Fixed by rotating and reframing the complete arena. No game-breaking failures remain in the tested paths.

The scripted full campaign: autopilot physically collected all 400 gold dots through Rapier sensors, cleared all five circuits and reached victory. The official two- and four-player AI Hub harness also passed latency, loss and host-leave cases.
Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank despite valid renderer and gameplay state. State assertions verified WebGPU; screenshots used the native WebGL2 backend for visual review.
engineFeedback: Three.js provided native toon node materials, orthographic composition and an animation mixer while allowing all art to be made directly in code.
Headless WebGPU capture was unreliable, so visual review used WebGL2 while the gameplay and protocol tests kept WebGPU. Input tests also needed to wait for actual frame sampling.
The arc-length lane network, buffered gap changes, rival behavior and the full arcade flow were custom game systems.
Coordinating fixed-step Rapier sensors with smooth lane transitions and the rendering/animation loop.
A smaller ready-made WebGPU toon/outline example with physics and headless validation would reduce integration work.
promptFeedback: The source research, controller-first design, attract mode and required live tuning tools gave the demo a clear arcade identity.
The relationship between standalone multiplayer and AI Hub multiplayer was open to interpretation; both are implemented.
Building and validating the full single-file package, multiple input methods and both multiplayer paths together.
Specify whether standalone internet multiplayer must use a hosted relay, manual signaling or an existing service, and provide an explicit browser support baseline.

aiHub.name: Dodge on Arrival
aiHub.tagline: Four lanes. Three lives. No brakes.
aiHub.description: Sweep gold from four looping lanes while rivals charge the other way. Queue last-second changes, squeeze through close calls and ink-slip out of trouble across five midnight circuits, or trade paint in local Bumper Tag and online ghost races.
aiHub.controls: Stick or A/D: inward/outward at gaps; R2/Cross or Space: gas; Square or Shift: ink slip; Options or Esc: pause. Driver 2: J/L, I, K. Touch: left swipe, right hold, contextual slip.
